title:
A heading in parsed Markdown. Note that in addition to normal headings, they may be used to define pages of tabbed content. A sequence of tab headings (at the same level) will be rendered as a tab group with the contents of each section as a tab and the title of the heading as the tab text. Tab groups may not nest, but it is fine to have normal headings within a tab (at deeper levels of nesting). ```md # Regular H1 Normal paragraph text. == First Content of tab 1. ### 1.1 More content of tab 1. == Second Content of tab 2. ## Regular H2 This section and its contents come _after_ the tab group. ``` == First Content of tab 1. ### 1.1 More content of tab 1. == Second Content of tab 2. == == It is also possible to end the last tab with a heading with no text (`== ==`) if the following text should be outside the tab (and there isn't a higher level header to end it naturally). Because HTML needs special handling to render as tabs, we add some extra elements that can be augmented for the CSS framework being used. - All tabs are surrounded by a `div` with class "tabset". - A `ul` is generated for the tab controls, each `li` with class "tab-handle". - The content of each tab is in a `div` with class "tab-content". - The tab content includes the original heading tag. ```html
  • First
  • Second

First

Content of tab 1.

1.1

More content of tab 1.

Second

Content of tab 2.

``` This structure can be transformed at rendering time to the needs of the CSS. For example, the server documentation micro-site transforms it into [Bootstrap tabs](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/3.3/javascript/#tabs). @see MarkdownNode
